question.prompt: For any real value of \(x\) the maximum value of \(8x-3x^2\) is:

solutions.explanation:
A real square is nonnegative, so writing the expression as a constant minus a square will reveal its maximum. Completing the square gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
8x-3x^2
&=-3\left[\left(x-\frac43\right)^2-\frac{16}{9}\right]\\
&=\frac{16}{3}-3\left(x-\frac43\right)^2.
\end{aligned}
\]
The subtracted term is nonnegative for every real \(x\), so the expression is at most \(\frac{16}{3}\). Equality occurs when \(x=\frac43\), making this bound attainable. The maximum is therefore \(\frac{16}{3}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).
solutions.title: Write a constant minus a square
